Trase's suite of products includes Origin, its agentic operating system; Leagues, its marketplace for specialized, configurable, ready-to-deploy agents; and Arena, where developers build, evaluate, and package the agents that run on Origin. With Jobber they can quote, schedule, invoice, and collect payments from their customers while providing an easy and professional customer experience. jobs.title: Senior Product Manager, Agent Growth
jobs.description: This a Full Remote job, the offer is available from: United States, Minnesota (USA) Lone Wolf builds the software real estate runs on. Brokerages, agents, MLSs, and associations across North America use our products for forms and transaction management (zipForm, Transaction Desk, Transact), e-signature (Authentisign), comparative market analysis (Cloud CMA), listing advertising (Boost), and brokerage back office. A large share of North American real estate agents use Lone Wolf products, and many of them buy on their own with a credit card: an e-signature plan, a forms upgrade, a CMA subscription, an ad for a new listing. You’ll be the owner that runs it as one system, with one dashboard and a steady stream of experiments along the way. You’ll wear two hats: • Product manager for Brand Management (Boost). Boost automates listing and brand advertising on Facebook, Instagram, and Google for agents and brokerages. You’ll own its roadmap, its metrics, and the priorities of its engineering team. • Growth lead for every agent-purchased product. You’ll own the path from first touch to purchase to expansion across Boost, Cloud CMA, Authentisign, zipForm and Transaction Desk upgrades, and more. This is your business to run. You’ll report to the Chief Innovation Officer, who sets direction, holds the number with the executive team, clears cross-functional blockers, and makes the calls that need executive weight: major pricing changes, tradeoffs across product pillars, and scale-or-stop decisions. Everything else is yours: the backlog, the experiments, the funnels, the roadmap, and the weekly review. You won’t be executing someone else’s plan. You’ll write it. This is a builder’s role with a wide surface. Most of the funnel runs through teams you won’t manage: marketing’s website and SEO, CX’s in-app messaging and onboarding, other product teams’ engineering time, and sales conversations with brokerages. Your leverage is data, speed, and the ability to bring people with you. Responsibilities: • Own the agent revenue number. Build the dashboard yourself (SQL, Metabase), run the weekly review, and make it what everyone else looks at. Bring a monthly readout to the executive team alongside the CIO. • Find and fix funnel leaks in landing pages, pricing pages, checkout, trials, and in-product upgrade prompts. • Run lifecycle email as a growth channel. Iterable triggers at listing events, onboarding, upgrade, and win-back. Write the copy, set up the tests, and read the results. • Ship your own variants. Build landing pages and messaging variants yourself with AI tools. Work hand in hand with Marketing’s website lead on lwolf.com agent pages and SEO, where Boost now sits alongside our other agent products. • Run experiments end to end: hypothesis, instrumentation, launch, readout, and decision, at a high tempo. • Own agent pricing and packaging: bundles, trials, annual plans, auto-renewal, and cross-product offers. Bring recommendations to the CIO for the big moves. • Shape how agents buy Transact. As agents move from zipForm and Transaction Desk to Transact, make sure the products they pay for today, like Authentisign and forms upgrades, still have a clear path to purchase. • Run the Boost roadmap. Balance growth work against reliability and commitments to brokerage and partner customers. Sales owns brokerage Boost deals; you make sure the product and the team behind it support them. • Test paid acquisition on a small budget, and scale only what pays back. • Get things done across the business. Win engineering time from other product teams, in-app placements from CX, page changes from Marketing, and agent offers in Sales conversations, without owning any of them. • Stand up lean product analytics that don’t require hand-instrumenting every event. Requirements: • A track record of growing a purchase funnel with a product-led mindset. Bring the before-and-after numbers and explain what you personally did to move them. • Range across disciplines.

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager, Self-Hosted and Connected Temporal
jobs.description: Role Summary Temporal is used by a lot of companies in a wide variety of contexts. Many use Temporal Cloud. Many others users don’t yet know about Temporal Cloud, believe self-hosting is cheaper, and/or just don’t yet see a need to move. Still others (often happily using Temporal Cloud at large scale) also operate environments where a managed service isn't an option today and may never be, like: • AI and application companies embedding Temporal inside software their own customers run in isolated, air-gapped environments, or offering a remote management BYOA posture • Large enterprises keeping operational control of critical systems in-house by policy • Companies operating in sovereign clouds and similar contexts where legal or organizational requirements make outside management difficult or impossible This role owns understanding the world of Temporal usage outside Cloud, what the different contexts demand, and where Temporal should (and shouldn't) engage. That includes what we build, what we support, what we charge for, and what we leave alone. You'll shape which offerings we pursue and how they make money or contribute to the larger business. Then you'll take the ones we commit to through launch and adoption. Open source Temporal is central to this. We’re investing heavily in OSS, from performance improvements to easier management to clearer guidance on compatibility and cost. When companies write their apps on Temporal, they’re making a huge bet on us, and that trust is sacred. A large part of this role is improving and shepherding how we keep making OSS better. What You’ll Do • Map usage outside Temporal Cloud. Build the company's clearest picture of where Temporal runs outside Cloud and why. Separate structural constraints (air gaps, regulation, owning operational risk) from cost, inertia, and/or other factors. Turn that into segments and use cases leadership can make decisions with. • Decide what we pursue. Recommend which needs deserve new offerings, which Temporal Cloud should cover, and which we deliberately leave alone. Write the case, defend it, and revisit it when the evidence changes. • Define the line between open source and paid. Set clear guidelines for which improvements and support go into open source Temporal, and where paid offerings take over. Keep the open source experience strong, and make the line easy for users and internal teams to understand. • Define the business model. Work with leadership, Sales, and Finance on packaging, pricing, and how we sell offerings that run outside our infrastructure. Know what customers will pay for and what it costs us to support it. • Help Cloud win where it should. Work with other PMs so workloads that can run on Cloud move there more easily, with a clear value and TCO case. • Lead without authority. Align Engineering, Resident Architects, Dev Success, Security, and go-to-market teams, including when their incentives conflict. • Own outcomes. Define success in terms of adoption, revenue, and retention. Use the results to steer further investment. What You’ll Bring • A track record of setting product strategy, not only executing it. You've spotted a new offering or market, made the case for it, and seen it through to revenue. • Experience with infrastructure or platform products that customers operate themselves: open source, on-prem, or hybrid. • Commercial judgment. You can connect a customer problem to willingness to pay, pricing, and the cost of delivering and supporting the product. • Technical depth in distributed systems and operations: Kubernetes, databases, replication, upgrades, and failure recovery. You can go deep with engineers and turn the tradeoffs into product decisions. • Comfort saying "not this" and backing it with evidence. You change course when the facts change. • Clear writing. You can turn messy evidence from customers and the field into a recommendation leaders can act on. Nice to Haves • Experience making money from open source or open-core pro

jobs.description: Caseware is one of Canadas original Fintech companies having led the global audit and accounting software industry for over 30 years with more than 500000 users across 130 countries and available in 16 different languages. While you might not have heard of us (yet) over 36000 accounting and audit professionals list Caseware as a skill on their LinkedIn profiles! Were looking for a Technical Product Manager to own how Caseware builds evaluates and raises the quality of AI across the platform. You are the product owner of our core AI surfaces: the agents and agent builder practitioners use to do real work the eval builder and eval roadmap that let us measure quality and the agentic memory that lets the platform improve as it is used. You decide what we build in what order and whether it clears the bar before it reaches someones audit file. You are also the closest thing the product has to a practitioner in the room. Acting as an SME proxy you carry the voice of the auditor into every decision: shadowing real workflows validating outputs against what a qualified practitioner would actually sign off on and turning this doesnt feel right into specific actionable failure modes. You partner closely with applied scientists engineering domain experts and external partner firms. You own the product outcome and the quality bar; the applied science team owns the science underneath it. This role demands high agency. Youll operate with real autonomy make decisions without waiting for permission and own the outcome success measured by results not activity. Youre intellectually curious collaborate easily across teams and take real pride in getting it right. This work sits in the financial audit and assurance domain. Independent audit is one of the quiet foundations of the global economy when investors lenders and regulators can trust that financial statements are accurate capital flows and markets function. That trust rests entirely on the quality of the work which is why the bar for AI here is so high. You dont need an accounting background to start though one or any real connection to the profession adds high value. What you do need is genuine curiosity about the complexity of auditing and a deep appreciation for why quality is non-negotiable.
